title: Follow the open descriptor through a private log rotation
goal: Show why rename-based rotation does not redirect an already-open writer, then reopen it and verify both retained log generations.
challenge: Use one private regular log, explicit private rotation state/config and one retained generation. Hold a writer descriptor across rotation, compare device/inode identities, and prove old-descriptor bytes land only in the rotated file. Reopen for new bytes; never rotate system logs.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/operations-rotationfd.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && saved_umask=$(umask) && umask 077 && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/operations-rotationfd.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; dir_ok() { test -d "$1" && test ! -L "$1" && test "$(realpath -e -- "$1")" = "$w/$1"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here && test "$(df --output=avail -k . | tail -1)" -gt 65536
steps.explanation: Create and record a new private guest workspace. Stop on any failed guard; the free-space check is an observation, not a guaranteed reserve. Do not use the host terminal.
steps.expected: A unique learner-owned mode0700 directory; no originals overwritten.

steps.command: here && test ! -L /proc/$$/fd/9 && test ! -e /proc/$$/fd/9 && fresh live.log live.log.1 rotate.conf rotate.state old-id.txt new-id.txt && printf 'BEFORE\n' > live.log && printf '%s\n' '"'"$w/live.log"'" {' 'rotate 1' 'size 1' 'create 0600 learner learner' '}' > rotate.conf && stat -c '%d:%i' live.log > old-id.txt && exec 9>>live.log
steps.explanation: One tiny cooperative fixture, no include/scripts/compression/copytruncate. Its directory and configuration are private.
steps.expected: Descriptor9 points to the current regular log inode.

steps.command: rotate_once() { here && fresh live.log.1 rotate.state new-id.txt && test -f live.log && test ! -L live.log && test "$(stat -c %d:%i live.log)" = "$(cat old-id.txt)" && test "$(readlink /proc/$$/fd/9)" = "$w/live.log" && timeout -k 1s 5s /usr/sbin/logrotate -f -s "$w/rotate.state" "$w/rotate.conf"; }; here && rotate_once && test -f live.log.1 && test ! -L live.log.1 && test "$(stat -c %d:%i live.log.1)" = "$(cat old-id.txt)" && stat -c '%d:%i' live.log > new-id.txt && ! cmp -s old-id.txt new-id.txt && printf 'OLD_FD\n' >&9 && grep -qx OLD_FD live.log.1 && test ! -s live.log
steps.explanation: Rename preserves the old inode while create supplies a new pathname inode. Force only this explicit private config/state.
steps.expected: Original inode is .1; descriptor9 appends there, not to the empty new file.

steps.command:
here && exec 9>&- && exec 9>>live.log && printf 'REOPENED
' >&9 && exec 9>&- && cmp live.log.1 <(printf 'BEFORE
OLD_FD
') && cmp live.log <(printf 'REOPENED
') && test "$(stat -c %U:%a live.log)" = learner:600
steps.explanation: A real daemon needs its own documented reopen mechanism; this shell demonstration explicitly closes/reopens its private descriptor. Never send broad signals.
steps.expected: Both generations match intended bytes; writer closed; new file learner0600.
